texts.title: Is it time to close city centres to cars?

paragraphs.text: Several European cities have closed parts of their centres to private cars, and the idea is now being discussed in many others. As someone who has lived in a car-free district for three years, I am generally in favour, although I do not think a complete ban suits every town.

The benefits I have noticed are real. The air feels cleaner, the streets are quieter, and children play outside in places that were once too dangerous. Local cafés have put tables on the pavement, and on summer evenings the neighbourhood is busier than it ever was when cars were allowed.

Shopkeepers were the strongest opponents of the plan. They feared that customers who could no longer park outside would go elsewhere. For some businesses, especially those selling heavy goods such as furniture, this fear was justified, and a few have moved away. Most, however, have kept their customers.

A ban only works if people have good alternatives. Our district is served by frequent trams, and there are cycle lanes on every main road. In a small town with one bus an hour, closing the centre to cars would simply cut residents off from shops and services.

Elderly and disabled residents deserve particular attention. Taxis and delivery vans are still permitted in our area at certain times, and I believe this flexibility is essential. A policy that makes life easier for the young and fit while trapping others at home cannot be called a success.

items.quote: I do not think a complete ban suits every town
items.prompt: The writer supports closing the centre to cars in every town.

explanation.en: The writer is “generally in favour” but adds “I do not think a complete ban suits every town”. “Every town” contradicts his view → NO.
explanation.kk: Автор «generally in favour», бірақ «I do not think a complete ban suits every town» деп қосады. «Every town» оның ұстанымына қайшы → NO.
explanation.ru: Автор «generally in favour», но добавляет «I do not think a complete ban suits every town». «Every town» противоречит его позиции → NO.

items.quote: As someone who has lived in a car-free district for three years
items.prompt: The writer says he has lived in a car-free area.

explanation.en: “As someone who has lived in a car-free district for three years” → YES. It is the writer’s own claim about himself.
explanation.kk: «As someone who has lived in a car-free district for three years» → YES. Бұл — автордың өзі туралы айтқаны.
explanation.ru: «As someone who has lived in a car-free district for three years» → YES. Это утверждение самого автора о себе.

items.prompt: The writer feels that the air in the district has become cleaner.

explanation.en: “The air feels cleaner” — one of the benefits the writer has noticed → YES.
explanation.kk: «The air feels cleaner» — автордың өзі байқаған артықшылықтың бірі → YES.
explanation.ru: «The air feels cleaner» — это одно из преимуществ, которые автор заметил сам → YES.

items.quote: the neighbourhood is busier than it ever was when cars were allowed
items.prompt: The writer thinks the neighbourhood is less lively than before the change.

explanation.en: “busier than it ever was when cars were allowed” — livelier than before. “Less lively” contradicts this → NO.
explanation.kk: «busier than it ever was when cars were allowed» — бұрынғыдан да жанды. «Less lively» бұған қайшы → NO.
explanation.ru: «busier than it ever was when cars were allowed» — оживлённее, чем раньше. «Less lively» противоречит → NO.

items.quote: For some businesses, especially those selling heavy goods such as furniture, this fear was justified
items.prompt: The writer accepts that the shopkeepers’ fears were justified for some businesses.

explanation.en: “For some businesses … this fear was justified” — the writer accepts this → YES.
explanation.kk: «For some businesses … this fear was justified» — автор мұны мойындайды → YES.
explanation.ru: «For some businesses … this fear was justified» — автор признаёт это → YES.

items.prompt: The writer thinks the council should pay compensation to businesses that moved away.

explanation.en: The writer reports that a few businesses moved away but says nothing about compensation or the council → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Автор бірнеше дүкен көшіп кеткенін айтады, бірақ өтемақы мен әкімдік туралы ештеңе айтпайды → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Автор сообщает, что несколько магазинов уехали, но о компенсации и совете не говорит ничего → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: Most, however, have kept their customers.
items.prompt: The writer claims that most businesses lost customers after the change.

explanation.en: “Most, however, have kept their customers” — most kept them → NO.
explanation.kk: «Most, however, have kept their customers» — көпшілігі сатып алушыларын сақтап қалған → NO.
explanation.ru: «Most, however, have kept their customers» — большинство сохранили покупателей → NO.

items.quote: A ban only works if people have good alternatives
items.prompt: The writer believes a ban needs good public transport to succeed.

explanation.en: “A ban only works if people have good alternatives”, with the example of trams versus one bus an hour → YES.
explanation.kk: «A ban only works if people have good alternatives» және трамвай мен сағатына бір автобус мысалы → YES.
explanation.ru: «A ban only works if people have good alternatives» и пример с трамваями и одним автобусом в час → YES.

items.quote: Our district is served by frequent trams
items.prompt: The writer considers trams to be a better choice than buses for any town.

explanation.en: The writer contrasts frequent trams with “one bus an hour” — the point is frequency, not the type of transport. There is no view that trams beat buses → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Автор жиі жүретін трамвай мен «one bus an hour» дегенді салыстырады — мәселе көлік түрінде емес, жиілігінде. Трамвай автобустан жақсы деген пікір жоқ → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Автор противопоставляет частые трамваи и «one bus an hour» — дело в частоте, а не в виде транспорта. Мнения, что трамвай лучше автобуса, нет → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: I believe this flexibility is essential
items.prompt: The writer thinks allowing taxis in at certain times is unnecessary.

explanation.en: About allowing taxis and vans the writer says: “I believe this flexibility is essential” — the opposite of “unnecessary” → NO.
explanation.kk: Такси мен жеткізу көлігін кіргізу туралы автор «I believe this flexibility is essential» дейді — «unnecessary» керісінше → NO.
explanation.ru: О допуске такси и доставки автор пишет: «I believe this flexibility is essential» — «unnecessary» противоположно → NO.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–10. Look at the text. Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer? Write YES if the statement agrees with the views of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the views of the writer, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
